text: Ichthyophthirius multifiliis, commonly known as white spot disease or ich, presents as small white cysts resembling salt grains on the skin, fins, and gills of freshwater fish. Affected fish often clamp their fins and rub against surfaces.
Fin rot is a bacterial infection causing frayed, discolored, or receding fins. It often occurs alongside poor water quality and stress. Early stages show white edges on fins.
Clamped fins can be a general sign of stress, poor water parameters, or early-stage parasitic infection like ich. Always test ammonia, nitrite, and nitrate levels first.
Velvet disease (Oodinium) appears as a fine gold or rust-colored dusting on the fish, often mistaken for ich but requires different treatment with copper-based medications.
